sections.title: Introduction and Greeting
observations: Paul introduces himself as an apostle of Christ Jesus, emphasizing his authority and the grace he has received.
He addresses Timothy as his beloved child, highlighting their close relationship and the personal nature of this letter.

sections.title: Encouragement to Timothy
observations: Paul expresses gratitude for Timothy's faith, which was passed down from his grandmother Lois and mother Eunice.
He encourages Timothy to fan into flame the gift of God, reminding him of the power, love, and self-discipline that comes from the Holy Spirit.

sections.title: Do Not Be Ashamed
observations: Paul urges Timothy not to be ashamed of the testimony about our Lord or of Paul’s imprisonment.
He calls Timothy to join in suffering for the gospel, emphasizing the importance of standing firm in faith.

sections.title: Guard the Good Deposit
observations: Paul instructs Timothy to guard the good deposit entrusted to him, which refers to the gospel and sound doctrine.
He reminds Timothy of the importance of relying on the Holy Spirit to help him in this task.

importantVerses.commentary: For God gave us a spirit not of fear but of power and love and self-control.
But I am not ashamed, for I know whom I have believed, and I am convinced that he is able to guard until that Day what has been entrusted to me.

questions: What does it mean to 'fan into flame' the gift of God?
How can we practically guard the good deposit of the gospel in our lives today?
In what ways can we encourage others to not be ashamed of the gospel?
